title: Path Traversal via path.resolve and fs APIs
platform_conditions: Node.js runtime (path and fs modules); behavior identical on POSIX and Windows with platform-specific separators
security_mechanism: path.resolve(base, userFile) treats an absolute second argument as a full replacement -- resolve('/var/data', '/etc/passwd') returns '/etc/passwd' -- and it normalizes '..' segments away without ever checking containment, so '../..' escapes silently. path.join keeps the base but still preserves '..' segments, so join alone is not a confinement mechanism either. Any fs call (readFile, createReadStream, unlink) then operates on the escaped path; symlink entries inside user-uploaded archives add a second escape once extracted.

source_sink_clues.source: Download/upload filename parameters, stored file names from user profiles, archive entry names, and any path fragment from a request.
source_sink_clues.sink: path.resolve / path.join over attacker input feeding fs.readFile, fs.createReadStream, fs.writeFile, fs.unlink, or archive member extraction

tracking_guards: Check the code strips to path.basename before composing, or normalizes the candidate and verifies path.resolve(candidate).startsWith(resolve(base) + sep) before any fs call; check symlinked entries in extracted archives are rejected or resolved and re-checked.
not_candidate_when: The path fragment is generated server-side (UUID/content hash), basename is taken and a realpath containment check runs before the fs call, or the resolved candidate is compared to a fixed allowlist of full paths.
synthetic_safe_example: const clean = path.basename(userFile); fs.readFile(path.join('/var/data', clean), cb);
public_references: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/22.html
